title: Why your morning routine keeps failing

slides.headline: Your routine isn't failing because you're **lazy**
slides.subhead: 3 reasons it keeps falling apart, and the fix for each
slides.notes: Cover = the reel's hook reframed as a promise. Keep under 10 words in the headline.

slides.headline: The 5 a.m. alarm. The cold plunge. The journal.
slides.body:
And by Thursday it's gone. Again.
It's not a discipline problem. It's a design problem.
slides.notes: Relatable tension: name the exact thing they tried.

slides.headline: 1. You copied **someone else's** routine
slides.body: Their mornings aren't your mornings. Start with one habit that already fits the morning you actually have.

slides.headline: 2. You made it **way too long**
slides.body: A 90-minute routine dies the first time you oversleep. Build a 10-minute version for bad days: the non-negotiable one.

slides.headline: 3. It starts **the night before**
slides.body: If you scroll until 1 a.m., no routine can save you. Pick a phone-down time and protect it like a meeting.

slides.headline: The fix, on one slide
items: Make it **yours**: one habit that already fits
Start **the night before**: phone down at a set time
slides.notes: Recap slide = the most saved slide. Make it screenshot-worthy.

slides.quote: A routine you can do on your **worst** day beats a perfect one you skip.

slides.headline: Save this for **tomorrow morning**
slides.body: Then tell me in the comments: which ONE habit would you keep?

caption:
Your morning routine isn't failing because you're lazy. It's failing because it was designed for someone else's life.

The three fixes:
1. Make it yours: start with one habit that already fits
2. Make it short: keep a 10-minute version for bad days
3. Start the night before: phone down at a set time

Save this for tomorrow morning. Which ONE habit would you keep? Tell me below.
